### Summary

When a Mesh's stages run as CUDA graphs, an exchange inside a stage cannot be captured: the meeting of the blocks
is host work. The exchange becomes a cut. The graph being captured is closed before it, the meeting runs on the
host, and a new graph opens after it, so the pack and the unpack stay inside graphs. All the blocks of the
process capture the same segments together, each on its own capture stream and its own worker stream, so their
cuts meet at the same rendezvous the same number of times. This is what lets split cubed-sphere panels and Meshes
of many blocks capture.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Turn an in-stage exchange into a host step between two graphs of a segment capture
(`exchange_cut`), and make every block of the Mesh capture the same segments (`align_captures`).

**Data.** In: the segment schedule of each block. Out: per segment, a list of steps (graph, host step, graph, ...).

**Placement.** Inside a segment capture of a Mesh with more than one block; at replay the host steps run between
the graphs.

**Activation.** `integration: execution` (default `auto`, which captures where nothing refuses; `cuda-graph`;
`eager`). Refused for more than one process and for an x1 split.

**Guarantee / limits.** A captured Mesh equals the same Mesh run eager bitwise (the tests below). A capture that
runs out of device memory stops the run with one error that names `execution: eager`.

**Evidence.** @sec-ch13-cuts-tests.
:::

The segment schedule and the graph rules of one block are @sec-ch11. This section adds what a Mesh needs on top of
them.

### Derivation

No equation: the cut is control flow. The property it has to keep is a count. In a segment capture each block runs
the segment three times eager on its capture stream (the warm-up) and once under capture, and every exchange
inside meets the other blocks at the rendezvous each time. If one block captured a segment while another did not,
the first would meet the rendezvous four times and the second once, and the Mesh would hang. `align_captures`
removes that case: a segment that any block has to (re)capture is dropped for every block before the stage runs, so
all of them capture it.

### Numerical method

`exchange_cut` takes the host step (the rendezvous or the communicator wait) and, optionally, what to run outside a
capture. Outside a segment capture, or when already inside a host step, it runs the plain launch. Inside one, it
closes the open graph, runs the host step, appends the host step to the segment's steps and opens the next graph;
at replay the steps run in order, graphs and host steps alternating. Its two callers are the block's exchange
launch (`MeshBlockImpl::launch_exchange`) and the panel-seam reconcile (`reconcile_panel_seams`). The captures of
a Mesh's blocks run concurrently in thread-local capture mode. Each block's capture stream and each worker stream
is an `OwnedStream`: lent to one owner at a time, given back when the owner is destroyed, never destroyed itself.
@fig-ch13-exchange-cut shows a segment with two cuts.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch13-exchange-cut
#| fig-cap: "A segment of two blocks with two in-stage exchanges. Under capture each exchange closes the open graph (blue boxes), runs its host step (the rendezvous, green) and opens the next graph; the pack and unpack stay inside the graphs. Both blocks meet at each host step, at the warm-up and at the capture alike."
#| fig-alt: "Two parallel lanes of boxes, graph, host step, graph, host step, graph, with dashed lines joining the two lanes at each host step."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch13.figures.fig_exchange_cut import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| the cut | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp exchange_cut >}} | `exchange_cut` | none |
| exchange launch as a cut | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::launch_exchange >}} | `launch_exchange` | none |
| seam reconcile as a cut | {{< code src/layout/seam_register.cpp reconcile_panel_seams >}} | `reconcile_panel_seams` | cubed sphere |
| capture together | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::align_captures >}} | `align_captures` | `execution` |
| a Mesh's stage | {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}} | `forward` | none |
| a segment's capture | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::capture >}} | `capture` | none |
| a segment's replay | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::replay >}} | `replay` | none |
| owned streams | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.hpp OwnedStream >}} | `OwnedStream` | none |
| refusals (ranks, x1 split) | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::config_reasons >}} | `config_reasons` | `nb1`, process group |
| capture out of memory | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::run_segments >}} | `run_segments` | none |

Walk-through: `MeshImpl::forward` calls `agree` (@sec-ch13-agree), then `align_captures`, then runs every
block's stage on the worker pool. A block's stage captures each segment whose graph is missing or stale and replays
it. A capture that runs out of device memory, in the warm-up, the capture or the graph instantiation, is rethrown
by `run_segments` as an out-of-memory error: "block $n$: a capture ran out of device memory; execution: eager runs
this deck", followed by the original message; every other error passes unchanged. The other blocks then leave their
waits (@sec-ch13-ghost). `config_reasons` refuses capture with more than one process ("multi-rank capture is not
done yet") and with an x1 split ("its relays inside the stage are not cut into segments yet").

### Tests {#sec-ch13-cuts-tests}

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_mesh_capture.cpp` (`test_mesh_capture.release`) | a captured Mesh equals the eager Mesh, every variable | exact (`torch::equal`, two checks) | the test source |
| `tests/test_mesh_capture_moist.py` (`test_mesh_capture_moist_python`) | the same with moist thermodynamics, FP64 and FP32 | exact (`torch.equal`) | the test source |
| `tests/test_cubed_sphere_capture.py` (`test_cubed_sphere_capture_python`) | a cubed-sphere Mesh with seam cuts equals eager over 10 steps | exact (`torch.equal`) | the test source |
| `tests/test_graph_mesh_many_blocks.py` (`test_graph_mesh_many_blocks_python`) | Meshes of 8, 24 and 40 blocks capture and equal eager | exact (`torch.equal`) | the test source |
| `tests/test_mesh_worker_streams.cpp` (`test_mesh_worker_streams.release`) | one worker stream per block, all distinct, none from torch's shared pool | exact (pass/fail) | the test source |

Evidence. On one CUDA device the 24- and 96-block cubed spheres of `tests/test_default_execution.py` captured
72 and 288 segments with 216 and 792 cuts and no eager stage, and the 40-block Mesh of
`test_graph_mesh_many_blocks` captured 120 segments; each equalled its eager run bitwise.[^cuts-counts] Not
re-run at the pin (missing evidence there); the commits after these runs do not change the capture path. All five
tests passed in a by-name ctest subset on a CUDA build before the pin.[^cuts-subset] They are CUDA tests; none
runs on more than one rank, which `config_reasons` refuses.

### Limits

Not captured: runs on more than one process and runs with an x1 split (both refused, so they run eager). The
capture streams are given back to a shared list when their owner is destroyed and may be lent to a later Mesh as
capture or worker streams; a tensor allocated on such a stream, read on another stream without `record_stream`,
and freed after the stream changed owner is not ordered after that read (a hypothesis, not observed; worker
streams were already reused this way before). A capture that runs out of memory stops the run rather than falling
back to eager. Switch combinations are in @sec-ch12-matrix.
